verdict.rationale: FireHydrant documents AI-generated incident summaries that start as soon as an incident is declared, can be tailored per audience, and can notify Slack when a new summary is generated. It also documents a Scribe that joins Zoom and Google Calendar incident bridges to capture discussions and decisions. However, nothing shows AI drafting live stakeholder or status updates during the incident: AI drafting is documented only for post-incident retrospectives, and `/fh update` notes appear to be written by people. Missing for 10: AI-drafted live incident or status-page updates, evidence that summaries refresh continuously as the incident evolves, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, AI writes the incident as it happens — live summaries, drafted updates, and scribed call notes — so responders respond instead of typing

citations.quote: Summaries are created as soon as an incident is declared, providing key information right from the start.
With our new Audiences feature, summaries can now be tailored to meet the specific needs of different stakeholder groups.
After enabling, the FireHydrant Scribe will be invited to your meetings to capture crucial discussions and decisions made during incident bridges
FireHydrant currently supports meeting transcription for our Google Calendar and Zoom integrations.
Dive into incidents with AI-generated summaries that provide a clear, concise overview of the situation.
